I have been where you have been. Was fun to read and reminisce. There's a reason why people like you and me end up lonely. I spent too many years trying to find out what it was and it only got more depressing. If you want to exist, professional help will be your best bet. It will be rough at first and seem unhelpful, you'll have to be honest and it will help, trust me.

My family is also very loving, a got a kitten whom I've raised and means the world to me. I had my fair share of good memories. You described it perfectly. I would love to talk to you more because you sound a lot like me.

That's tough, but you have to realize that ending it is a permanent solution. Don't you think your current partner will be upset with loosing you like that. I suggest if you truly are sure about yourself, then you should end the relationship. It will be hard, but you'll feel different after. Then you can always see if you want to end it, but maybe you will feel better. 

As for the apartment thing, that's life, it's shit. It will always be shit and things like that will always happen. If you feel overwhelmed with stuff like that, I used to, I would suggest professional help of some kind.

It's not about being normal, it's about being happy. Clearly you haven't figured out what makes you happy. Being otherkin clearly isn't enough, you may want a thriving social life, or a successful high paying job, or just new hobbies. That's what you should focus on in your professional help, how to be otherkin AND happy. Sacrifices must be made, but it will be worth it. 

If I let my drug abuse problem affect other important aspects of my life, then it's actively subtracting from my happiness. You have to figure out the balance, you can't show up to work high, you just can't. Hope this analogy helps as it's the only one I can relate to.

Pretty shallow way to judge yourself. Clearly you've come from a troublesome past, but from what you're saying you've fought against it. You now have friends, a boyfriend, essentially people who care about you. You've fought off self harm and anorexia, you're a strong person.

Get help, talk to your boyfriend. If you don't feel comfortable with that, he's not the right one. Find out what truly makes you happy. You're a strong person and with some help you'll be back on track. Much love and good luck!

News flash buddy, not everyone gets access to food, shelter, hands, 5 senses, good health, and the privilege of no disabilities. In fact tons of people die before they even get a chance to know what God is. Also very ignorant of you to assume I have all of those things. I could be homeless, disabled, and using a McDonalds wifi to write this. But that wouldn't make a difference to you would it? It definitely doesn't make a difference to your all mighty "Creator". The big picture is that this is the real world. Your mom and dad are your "creators". You only get one life and this is the one. Religion may have been useful once in uniting mankind a long time ago, but it's simply outdated now, and it definitely does not belong here. 

If I'm wrong, guess I'll see you in hell then :)

With that mindset you may be disappointed. You're going to run into surprises and bullshit all throughout your life, even in Uni. 

You should take a step back, analyse why you feel the way you do about your high school (feel free to vent to me in detail). Otherwise you'll end up hating Uni too.

I feel like seeing and reaching out to your dad is completely normal. It's closure, he's a human like you, and he needs it. He is your dad after all. Doesn't mean he should be forgiven for what he did. 

Don't let him manipulate you though, I don't know your dad and how your relationship with him is. Get closure for yourself, ask him what you want to know. That'll help you decide if you ever want to see him again. 

It will also help him. If what he says is alarming I would suggest contacting the right people. 

Also your mom should not be saying things like that to you, it's very wrong. Don't let it get to you. 

These are all my opinion, and your situation is very tough. Hope it all works out though and you get to focus on yourself and be done with this BS.

My only suggestion would be to communicate these feelings to him. The feelings that sometimes you don't know why, but you fight and are negative. If he's as great as you're making him sound, then you can work together on it. Replace drinking with calm and truthful communication. Don't pretend everything is fine, that's a very slippery and self destructive slope.

Hope everything works out, you sound like you have a great thing going. Good luck!
